observation.visible_scene: A demolition site showing the skeletal frame of a multi-story concrete building with graffiti-covered columns, exposed rebar and rubble on the floor slabs. Two machines are present: a yellow CAT excavator in the lower-left foreground (only its boom/arm visible, largely idle) and an orange long-reach excavator on the right whose hydraulic shear/attachment is positioned at the top edge of the structure, working on the upper floor. A plume of dust and small debris drifts downward through the open interior throughout the clip. The camera viewpoint is fixed on the building.
visible_changes: A continuous stream of dust/fine debris falls from the upper floor near the orange excavator's shear across the entire excerpt, indicating active cutting/tearing at that point.

A discrete chunk of concrete becomes visible around frame 17 in the upper interior and descends vertically through the open floors, reaching the lower portion of the frame by the last sample (a clear falling translation, not a new object).
The orange boom and shear make small positional adjustments at the top edge of the building (slight lowering/rotation of the wrist), consistent with ongoing work rather than a single strike.
The left yellow CAT arm stays essentially stationary relative to the building frame.
Background columns and floor slabs hold their positions, so the apparent motion is object motion, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The instant and cause of the falling chunk's detachment (it is already in the air when first seen).
Whether the building ultimately collapses or how much more is removed; outcomes beyond the crop are unseen.
Operator inputs and the full machine bodies (the orange excavator's cab/base and the CAT's body are partly out of frame).
uncertain_details: The magnitude of the orange arm's movement is subtle and could partly be vibration rather than deliberate repositioning.
A separate, stationary concrete fragment clings to a mid-left column and should not be confused with the falling chunk.
Dust density varies frame-to-frame; exact material identities of falling pieces cannot be confirmed.
